decisions.reason: Its two-component spraying technology is close to the firm's existing know-how, allowing early market signals to be interpreted and product improvements made.
The field-test result and dedicated page show the firm can assimilate feedback from a related injection pump application, making drop unlikely.
Reusing proven air motors means the firm already holds the key component knowledge, lowering the risk of dropping this low-pressure pump.
Fire protection flow monitoring is outside the firm's core pump/spraying knowledge, so early results are hard to interpret and improvement is less likely, favoring a drop.
Hydraulic two-component spraying builds on the firm's established two-component systems, and the development is recent enough to keep while learning.
